-- LEARN(sql.modeling.denormalize): a copy is fine once you know what keeps it honest.
CREATE TABLE test_cases (
  id          int  PRIMARY KEY,
  code        text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  -- Denormalized: derivable from test_runs, stored so the list needs no join.
  last_result text,
  last_run_on date
);
CREATE TABLE test_runs (
  id           int  PRIMARY KEY,
  test_case_id int  NOT NULL REFERENCES test_cases,
  run_on       date NOT NULL,
  result       text NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO test_cases (id, code) VALUES (1, 'TC-1'), (2, 'TC-2');

-- The one write path: record the run and move the copy forward, atomically.
WITH run AS (
  INSERT INTO test_runs VALUES (100, 1, '2026-11-02', 'failed')
  RETURNING test_case_id, run_on, result
)
UPDATE test_cases c
SET last_result = run.result, last_run_on = run.run_on
FROM run
WHERE c.id = run.test_case_id
  AND (c.last_run_on IS NULL OR c.last_run_on <= run.run_on);

-- A bulk import that doesn't know about the copy.
INSERT INTO test_runs VALUES (101, 1, '2026-11-09', 'passed'), (102, 2, '2026-11-09', 'passed');

-- Reconcile: recompute from the source and list where the copy disagrees.
CREATE VIEW latest_runs AS
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (test_case_id) test_case_id, run_on, result
  FROM test_runs
  ORDER BY test_case_id, run_on DESC, id DESC;

SELECT c.code, c.last_result AS stored, l.result AS actual
FROM test_cases c
LEFT JOIN latest_runs l ON l.test_case_id = c.id
WHERE c.last_result IS DISTINCT FROM l.result
ORDER BY c.code;

-- Repair from the same definition.
UPDATE test_cases c
SET last_result = l.result, last_run_on = l.run_on
FROM latest_runs l
WHERE l.test_case_id = c.id;
SELECT code, last_result, last_run_on FROM test_cases ORDER BY code;

-- Copying a value at the moment of an event records a different fact:
-- what was agreed then. That is not redundancy.
CREATE TABLE products (
  sku     text PRIMARY KEY,
  name    text NOT NULL,
  price   numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,
  vat_pct int NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE order_lines (
  order_id   int,
  sku        text REFERENCES products,
  qty        int NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0),
  unit_price numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,       -- the price on the order
  vat_pct    int NOT NULL,                  -- the KDV rate that applied
  -- Derived within the row: the database computes it, so it can't drift.
  net_total  numeric(12, 2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (qty * unit_price) STORED,
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, sku)
);
INSERT INTO products VALUES ('usb-c', 'USB-C kablo', 129.00, 18);

-- Order 1: copy price and rate from the product as part of the write.
INSERT INTO order_lines (order_id, sku, qty, unit_price, vat_pct)
SELECT 1, sku, 2, price, vat_pct FROM products WHERE sku = 'usb-c';

-- Later: a new price list, and the general KDV rate goes from 18 to 20.
UPDATE products SET price = 149.00, vat_pct = 20 WHERE sku = 'usb-c';

-- The order as invoiced, next to what a join to today's product says.
SELECT l.order_id, l.qty, l.unit_price, l.vat_pct, l.net_total,
       p.price AS price_today, p.vat_pct AS vat_today,
       l.qty * p.price AS net_if_joined
FROM order_lines l
JOIN products p USING (sku)
ORDER BY l.order_id;

-- LEARN(sql.modeling.temporal): a key that holds at every point in time, not just now.
-- = on an int column inside a GiST index needs btree_gist.
CREATE EXTENSION btree_gist;

-- Who owns which requirement, and when. valid_at is the business period.
CREATE TABLE requirement_owners (
  requirement_id int,
  owner          text NOT NULL,
  valid_at       daterange,
  PRIMARY KEY (requirement_id, valid_at WITHOUT OVERLAPS)   -- PG 18
);
INSERT INTO requirement_owners VALUES
  (1, 'Ayşe',   '[2026-01-01,2026-06-01)'),
  (1, 'Mehmet', '[2026-06-01,)'),            -- no upper bound: until further notice
  (2, 'Zeynep', '[2026-03-01,)');

-- As of a date: who owned what on 15 March?
SELECT requirement_id, owner
FROM requirement_owners
WHERE valid_at @> date '2026-03-15'
ORDER BY requirement_id;

-- Can takes over requirement 2 on 1 October: close the open row, then
-- open a new one. In the other order the INSERT would overlap.
UPDATE requirement_owners
SET valid_at = daterange(lower(valid_at), '2026-10-01')
WHERE requirement_id = 2 AND valid_at @> date '2026-10-01';
INSERT INTO requirement_owners VALUES (2, 'Can', '[2026-10-01,)');

SELECT requirement_id, owner, valid_at
FROM requirement_owners
ORDER BY requirement_id, lower(valid_at);

-- The key is a GiST index, like an exclusion constraint's.
SELECT c.relname AS index_name, am.amname AS method
FROM pg_index i
JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid
JOIN pg_am am   ON am.oid = c.relam
WHERE i.indrelid = 'requirement_owners'::regclass;

-- Two owners of requirement 1 during May: the periods overlap.
INSERT INTO requirement_owners VALUES (1, 'Selin', '[2026-05-01,2026-07-01)');

CREATE EXTENSION btree_gist;

-- Project versions over time. Project 1 was renamed on 1 July, so it has
-- two rows; project 2 was closed at the end of March.
CREATE TABLE projects (
  id       int,
  name     text NOT NULL,
  valid_at daterange,
  PRIMARY KEY (id, valid_at WITHOUT OVERLAPS)
);
INSERT INTO projects VALUES
  (1, 'Checkout',      '[2026-01-01,2026-07-01)'),
  (1, 'Payments',      '[2026-07-01,)'),
  (2, 'Legacy import', '[2026-01-01,2026-04-01)');

-- A membership must lie within its project's lifetime: a temporal FK.
CREATE TABLE memberships (
  project_id int,
  member     text,
  valid_at   daterange,
  PRIMARY KEY (project_id, member, valid_at WITHOUT OVERLAPS),
  FOREIGN KEY (project_id, PERIOD valid_at)
    REFERENCES projects (id, PERIOD valid_at)
);
INSERT INTO memberships VALUES
  -- Spans the rename: neither version covers it alone, both together do.
  (1, 'Ayşe', '[2026-03-01,2026-09-01)'),
  (2, 'Can',  '[2026-02-01,2026-04-01)');

-- A temporal join: match on the key and on overlapping periods, and
-- keep the intersection (*) as the period the combined row is true for.
SELECT m.member, p.name AS project, m.valid_at * p.valid_at AS during
FROM memberships m
JOIN projects p ON p.id = m.project_id AND p.valid_at && m.valid_at
ORDER BY m.member, lower(m.valid_at * p.valid_at);

-- Can stays on project 2 after it closed: nothing covers April to June.
INSERT INTO memberships VALUES (2, 'Can', '[2026-04-01,2026-07-01)');

-- LEARN(sql.modeling.anti-patterns): designs that hide the schema from the database.
-- EAV: one row per (entity, attribute, value), so any attribute "fits".
CREATE TABLE test_cases (id int PRIMARY KEY, code text NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE test_case_attrs (
  test_case_id int  REFERENCES test_cases,
  attr         text,
  value        text,                -- every type becomes text
  PRIMARY KEY (test_case_id, attr)
);
INSERT INTO test_cases VALUES (1, 'TC-1'), (2, 'TC-2'), (3, 'TC-3');
INSERT INTO test_case_attrs VALUES
  (1, 'priority', '1'), (1, 'automated', 'true'),
  (2, 'priority', 'high'),          -- not a number: accepted
  (3, 'prority',  '2');             -- misspelled attribute: accepted

-- Reading it back as a row takes one aggregate per attribute (a pivot).
SELECT c.code,
       max(a.value) FILTER (WHERE a.attr = 'priority')  AS priority,
       max(a.value) FILTER (WHERE a.attr = 'automated') AS automated
FROM test_cases c
LEFT JOIN test_case_attrs a ON a.test_case_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.code
ORDER BY c.code;

-- The attributes everyone has, as columns: types, NOT NULL, CHECK and
-- DEFAULT work again. jsonb keeps the per-customer extras.
CREATE TABLE test_cases_typed (
  id        int PRIMARY KEY,
  code      text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  priority  smallint NOT NULL CHECK (priority BETWEEN 1 AND 4),
  automated boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  extra     jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);
INSERT INTO test_cases_typed (id, code, priority, automated, extra)
VALUES (1, 'TC-1', 1, true, '{"browser": "Firefox"}');
SELECT code, priority, automated, extra ->> 'browser' AS browser FROM test_cases_typed;

INSERT INTO test_cases_typed (id, code, priority) VALUES (2, 'TC-2', 'high');

-- LEARN(sql.modern.16-to-18): three PG 18 features in two table definitions.
-- WITHOUT OVERLAPS needs GiST equality for the int column: btree_gist.
CREATE EXTENSION btree_gist;

-- Temporal primary key: many rows per requirement, but no two periods overlap.
CREATE TABLE requirement_versions (
  requirement_id int,
  valid          daterange,
  title          text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (requirement_id, valid WITHOUT OVERLAPS)
);
INSERT INTO requirement_versions VALUES
  (1, '[2026-01-01,2026-06-01)', 'Giriş'),
  (1, '[2026-06-01,)',           'Giriş, SSO dahil');

CREATE TABLE test_runs (
  id             uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),   -- time-ordered UUID
  requirement_id int  NOT NULL,
  ran            daterange NOT NULL,
  duration_ms    int  NOT NULL,
  duration_s     numeric(6,2) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (duration_ms / 1000.0),  -- virtual
  -- Temporal foreign key: the requirement must exist for the whole period.
  FOREIGN KEY (requirement_id, PERIOD ran)
    REFERENCES requirement_versions (requirement_id, PERIOD valid)
);
INSERT INTO test_runs (requirement_id, ran, duration_ms) VALUES
  (1, '[2026-03-10,2026-03-11)', 1500),
  (1, '[2026-05-31,2026-06-02)', 2250);  -- spans both versions: still covered

SELECT uuid_extract_version(id) AS uuid_version, ran, duration_ms, duration_s
FROM test_runs
ORDER BY ran;

-- The catalog: a GiST index behind the temporal key, NOT NULL as a
-- constraint row (contype n), and a virtual generated column.
SELECT c.conrelid::regclass AS tbl, c.conname, c.contype,
       CASE c.contype WHEN 'p' THEN am.amname END AS key_index
FROM pg_constraint c
LEFT JOIN pg_class i ON i.oid = c.conindid
LEFT JOIN pg_am am ON am.oid = i.relam
WHERE c.conrelid IN ('requirement_versions'::regclass, 'test_runs'::regclass)
ORDER BY c.conrelid::regclass::text, c.conname;
SELECT attname, attgenerated FROM pg_attribute
WHERE attrelid = 'test_runs'::regclass AND attgenerated <> '';

-- An overlapping period is rejected like an exclusion-constraint conflict.
INSERT INTO requirement_versions VALUES (1, '[2026-05-01,2026-07-01)', 'Çakışan');

CREATE TABLE test_cases (code text PRIMARY KEY, status text NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO test_cases VALUES ('TC-1', 'passed'), ('TC-2', 'failed'), ('TC-3', 'failed');

-- PG 16: IS JSON checks text before you cast it.
SELECT doc, doc IS JSON OBJECT AS is_object
FROM (VALUES ('{"case": "TC-1"}'), ('[1, 2]'), ('{"case": ')) AS v(doc)
ORDER BY doc;

-- A CI job reports its results as one JSON document.
CREATE TABLE ci_reports (id int PRIMARY KEY, body jsonb NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO ci_reports VALUES (1, '{"results": [
  {"case": "TC-1", "status": "passed"},
  {"case": "TC-2", "status": "passed"},
  {"case": "TC-4", "status": "failed"}]}');

-- PG 17: JSON_TABLE turns the document into rows.
SELECT r.*
FROM ci_reports,
     JSON_TABLE(body, '$.results[*]'
       COLUMNS (code text PATH '$.case', status text PATH '$.status')) AS r
ORDER BY r.code;

-- PG 17: MERGE with WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE and RETURNING merge_action();
-- PG 18: old/new in RETURNING.
WITH changes AS (
  MERGE INTO test_cases t
  USING (SELECT r.* FROM ci_reports,
           JSON_TABLE(body, '$.results[*]'
             COLUMNS (code text PATH '$.case', status text PATH '$.status')) AS r
         WHERE ci_reports.id = 1) AS r
  ON t.code = r.code
  WHEN MATCHED AND t.status <> r.status THEN UPDATE SET status = r.status
  WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT VALUES (r.code, r.status)
  WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN UPDATE SET status = 'not run'
  RETURNING merge_action() AS action, t.code, old.status AS old_status, new.status AS new_status
)
SELECT * FROM changes ORDER BY code;

-- LEARN(sql.modifying.insert-update): one statement per set of rows, not one per row.
CREATE TABLE products (
  id     int GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  sku    text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  name   text NOT NULL,
  price  numeric(10,2) NOT NULL CHECK (price > 0),
  active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true
);

-- Multi-row VALUES: one statement, one round trip, one transaction.
-- Always list the columns: the table's column order is not your API.
INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price) VALUES
  ('TEA-01', 'Rize çayı 1 kg',     210.00),
  ('COF-01', 'Türk kahvesi 250 g', 145.00),
  ('LOK-01', 'Lokum 500 g',        180.00);

-- DEFAULT is a value you can write, per row.
INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price, active) VALUES
  ('HEL-01', 'Tahin helvası', 120.00, DEFAULT),
  ('KUR-01', 'Kuruyemiş',     260.00, false);

-- How Go or TS code sends N rows without building SQL text: one array
-- per column (literals here; $1, $2, $3 from pgx), zipped by unnest.
INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price)
SELECT *
FROM unnest(ARRAY['SIM-01', 'POG-01'],
            ARRAY['Simit', 'Poğaça'],
            ARRAY[15.00, 25.00]::numeric[]);

-- The identity column drew one value per inserted row from its sequence.
SELECT id, sku, name, price, active FROM products ORDER BY id;

CREATE TABLE products (
  sku    text PRIMARY KEY,
  name   text NOT NULL,
  price  numeric(10,2) NOT NULL,
  active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true
);
INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price) VALUES ('TEA-01', 'Rize çayı 1 kg', 210.00);

-- A supplier's CSV landed in a staging table as raw text, Turkish
-- number format included (decimal comma, dot for thousands).
CREATE TABLE staging (sku text, name text, price_text text);
INSERT INTO staging VALUES
  ('BAK-01', 'Fıstıklı baklava 1 kg', '1.250,00'),
  ('SIM-01', 'Simit',                 '15,00'),
  ('TEA-01', 'Rize çayı (dup)',       '1,00');

-- INSERT ... SELECT: convert, filter and insert in one statement.
-- New products start inactive; skus we already sell are skipped.
INSERT INTO products (sku, name, price, active)
SELECT s.sku,
       s.name,
       replace(replace(s.price_text, '.', ''), ',', '.')::numeric,
       false
FROM staging s
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM products p WHERE p.sku = s.sku);

SELECT sku, name, price, active FROM products ORDER BY sku;

-- LEARN(sql.querying.select): pick columns, filter rows, and know when each clause runs.
CREATE TABLE products (
  id       int PRIMARY KEY,
  name     text NOT NULL,
  category text NOT NULL,
  price    numeric(10,2) NOT NULL,
  stock    int NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO products VALUES
  (1, 'Çay bardağı seti', 'kitchen',  189.90, 40),
  (2, 'Cezve',            'kitchen',  349.00,  0),
  (3, 'Kilim yastık',     'home',     520.00, 12),
  (4, 'Bakır tepsi',      'kitchen',  899.00,  3),
  (5, 'Termos',           'outdoor',  649.00, 25),
  (6, 'Hamak',            'outdoor', 1150.00,  0);

-- Name the columns you need; computed columns get an alias.
SELECT name, price, price * stock AS stock_value
FROM products
WHERE category = 'kitchen' AND stock > 0
ORDER BY stock_value DESC;

-- AND binds tighter than OR. This reads as
-- "outdoor (any stock) OR (kitchen AND in stock)": Hamak sneaks in.
SELECT name FROM products
WHERE category = 'outdoor' OR category = 'kitchen' AND stock > 0
ORDER BY id;

-- What was meant. IN is a list of ORs, and it spares you the parentheses.
SELECT name FROM products
WHERE category IN ('outdoor', 'kitchen') AND stock > 0
ORDER BY id;

-- BETWEEN includes both ends: 349.00 and 649.00 both match.
SELECT name, price FROM products
WHERE price BETWEEN 349 AND 649
ORDER BY price;

-- WHERE runs before the SELECT list exists, so its aliases don't either.
SELECT name, price * stock AS stock_value
FROM products
WHERE stock_value > 5000;

CREATE TABLE events (
  id        serial PRIMARY KEY,
  title     text NOT NULL,
  kind      text NOT NULL,
  starts_at timestamp NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO events (title, kind, starts_at) VALUES
  ('Deploy window', 'ops',    '2026-11-12 09:00:00'),
  ('Istanbul meetup', 'talk', '2026-11-12 18:30:00'),
  ('istanbul study group', 'talk', '2026-11-13 19:00:00'),
  ('Quiet day', 'other', '2026-11-14 12:00:00');

-- Case-insensitive search: ILIKE lowercases both sides, then matches.
SELECT title FROM events WHERE title ILIKE '%istanbul%';

-- Conditional labels: searched CASE, NULL when nothing matches (no ELSE).
SELECT title,
       CASE WHEN kind = 'ops'  THEN 'maintenance'
            WHEN kind = 'talk' THEN 'community'
       END AS label
FROM events
ORDER BY id;

-- to_char renders timestamps the way reports want them.
SELECT title, to_char(starts_at, 'Dy DD Mon HH24:MI') AS when
FROM events
ORDER BY starts_at;
files.sql/search/01-fts/examples/01_tsvector_t:
-- LEARN(sql.search.fts): a document becomes lexemes, a query becomes lexemes and operators.
SELECT to_tsvector('english',
  'Exports must include every linked test case; signed exports are archived.') AS document;

-- Four ways to build a query. Only to_tsquery reads operators from its input.
SELECT to_tsquery('english', 'export & (sign | archive)')            AS to_tsquery,
       plainto_tsquery('english', 'signed exports')                  AS plainto,
       phraseto_tsquery('english', 'linked test case')               AS phraseto,
       websearch_to_tsquery('english', '"test case" export -draft')  AS websearch;

-- @@ asks: does this document satisfy this query?
SELECT q AS typed,
       to_tsvector('english', 'Exports must include every linked test case')
         @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', q) AS matches
FROM (VALUES ('exported cases'), ('"linked test"'), ('"test linked"'),
             ('export -linked')) AS t(q);

-- Type-ahead needs prefixes (:*), and a prefix goes through the stemmer too.
SELECT q AS typed,
       to_tsvector('english', 'Database migrations run at startup')
         @@ to_tsquery('english', q) AS english,
       to_tsvector('simple', 'Database migrations run at startup')
         @@ to_tsquery('simple', q) AS simple
FROM (VALUES ('migr:*'), ('migrati:*'), ('migration:*')) AS t(q);

-- to_tsquery is a query language, not a search box.
SELECT to_tsquery('english', 'signed exports');
files.sql/search/01-fts/examples/02_ranking.sq:
CREATE TABLE requirements (
  code  text PRIMARY KEY,
  title text NOT NULL,
  body  text NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO requirements VALUES
  ('REQ-1', 'Audit log export', 'Administrators download the full log as CSV.'),
  ('REQ-2', 'Signed reports', 'Each report export is signed and noted in the audit log.'),
  ('REQ-3', 'Data retention', 'An export runs nightly. Records older than a year are '
            'deleted, and every deletion is recorded in the audit trail.'),
  ('REQ-4', 'Password reset', 'Reset links expire after an hour; the audit log keeps each request.');

-- The same words, ranked three ways. Ranks are floats: round them for display.
SELECT code,
       round(ts_rank(flat, q)::numeric, 4)    AS rank_flat,
       round(ts_rank(doc, q)::numeric, 4)     AS rank_weighted,
       round(ts_rank_cd(doc, q)::numeric, 4)  AS rank_cd
FROM requirements,
     websearch_to_tsquery('english', 'audit export') AS q,
     LATERAL (SELECT to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || body) AS flat,
                     setweight(to_tsvector('english', title), 'A') ||
                     setweight(to_tsvector('english', body), 'B') AS doc) AS v
WHERE doc @@ q
ORDER BY rank_weighted DESC, code;

-- ts_headline re-reads the original text and marks what matched.
SELECT code,
       ts_headline('english', body, websearch_to_tsquery('english', 'audit export'),
                   'StartSel=[, StopSel=], MaxFragments=2, MaxWords=6, MinWords=3')
         AS snippet
FROM requirements
WHERE code IN ('REQ-2', 'REQ-3')
ORDER BY code;
files.sql/search/01-fts/examples/03_stored_gin:
-- The tsvector is computed on write and kept: STORED is required to index it.
CREATE TABLE requirements (
  id     int PRIMARY KEY,
  title  text NOT NULL,
  body   text NOT NULL,
  search tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
           setweight(to_tsvector('english', title), 'A') ||
           setweight(to_tsvector('english', body), 'B')) STORED
);
INSERT INTO requirements (id, title, body)
SELECT g,
       (ARRAY['Audit log export', 'Password reset', 'Signed reports',
              'Bulk import', 'Session timeout'])[g % 5 + 1] || ' ' || g,
       (ARRAY['Every change is written to the audit log.',
              'Users can export the results as CSV.',
              'Reset links expire after one hour.',
              'Imports validate every row first.'])[g % 4 + 1]
FROM generate_series(1, 20000) AS g;
SELECT title, body, search FROM requirements WHERE id = 5;
CREATE INDEX requirements_search ON requirements USING gin (search);
ANALYZE requirements;

-- Top 5 by rank: the index finds every match, then each one is ranked.
EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF)
SELECT id, title
FROM requirements, websearch_to_tsquery('english', 'audit export') AS q
WHERE search @@ q
ORDER BY ts_rank(search, q) DESC, id
LIMIT 5;

SELECT count(*) AS matches
FROM requirements
WHERE search @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', 'audit export');

SELECT id, title, round(ts_rank(search, q)::numeric, 4) AS rank
FROM requirements, websearch_to_tsquery('english', 'audit export') AS q
WHERE search @@ q
ORDER BY ts_rank(search, q) DESC, id
LIMIT 5;

-- LEARN(sql.search.turkish): the configuration decides what a word becomes.
SELECT cfg, to_tsvector(cfg, 'Raporlar İstanbul''da hazırlandı ve testleri bitti') AS document
FROM unnest(ARRAY['turkish', 'english', 'simple']::regconfig[]) AS cfg;

CREATE TABLE requirements (
  id     int PRIMARY KEY,
  title  text NOT NULL,
  search tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('turkish', title)) STORED
);
INSERT INTO requirements (id, title) VALUES
  (1, 'Test raporları PDF olarak indirilebilir'),
  (2, 'Haftalık rapor e-posta ile gönderilir'),
  (3, 'Şifreler en az on iki karakter olmalı');

-- This server's default; initdb chose it from the locale.
SET LOCAL default_text_search_config = 'pg_catalog.english';

-- The column holds turkish stems. Which rows does each query find?
SELECT q AS typed,
       (SELECT string_agg(id::text, ',' ORDER BY id) FROM requirements
         WHERE search @@ plainto_tsquery('turkish', q)) AS turkish,
       (SELECT string_agg(id::text, ',' ORDER BY id) FROM requirements
         WHERE search @@ plainto_tsquery(q)) AS no_config,
       (SELECT string_agg(id::text, ',' ORDER BY id) FROM requirements
         WHERE search @@ plainto_tsquery('simple', q)) AS simple
FROM (VALUES ('rapor'), ('raporlar'), ('raporları'), ('şifre'), ('şifreler')) AS t(q);

-- to_tsvector lowercases with the database's rules (here C.UTF-8: I -> i, never ı).
SELECT spelling,
       to_tsvector('turkish', spelling)                           AS default_lower,
       to_tsvector('turkish', lower(spelling COLLATE "tr-x-icu")) AS turkish_lower
FROM unnest(ARRAY['IĞDIR', 'Iğdır', 'ığdır', 'ISPARTA', 'ısparta', 'İZMİR', 'IZMIR'])
     AS spelling;

-- A COLLATE on the input doesn't help: only lower() reads the collation.
SELECT to_tsvector('turkish', 'ISPARTA' COLLATE "tr-x-icu") AS collate_ignored;

-- Lowercase the Turkish way on both sides: in the stored column and in the query.
CREATE TABLE news (
  id       int PRIMARY KEY,
  headline text NOT NULL,
  search   tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
             to_tsvector('turkish', lower(headline COLLATE "tr-x-icu"))) STORED
);
INSERT INTO news (id, headline) VALUES
  (1, 'IĞDIR''DA YENİ HAVALİMANI AÇILDI'),
  (2, 'Iğdır kayısısı Avrupa yolunda'),
  (3, 'Isparta''da gül hasadı başladı');

SELECT q AS typed,
       (SELECT string_agg(id::text, ',' ORDER BY id) FROM news
         WHERE search @@ plainto_tsquery('turkish', q)) AS raw_query,
       (SELECT string_agg(id::text, ',' ORDER BY id) FROM news
         WHERE search @@ plainto_tsquery('turkish', lower(q COLLATE "tr-x-icu")))
         AS turkish_lowered_query
FROM (VALUES ('ığdır'), ('IĞDIR'), ('Iğdır'), ('ISPARTA'), ('igdir')) AS t(q);

-- Snowball's turkish stemmer strips suffixes by rule, without a dictionary.
SELECT word, to_tsvector('turkish', word) AS lexeme
FROM unnest(ARRAY['rapor', 'raporlar', 'raporları',
                  'hata', 'hatalar', 'hatası',
                  'gereksinim', 'gereksinimler', 'gereksinimleri']) AS word;

-- Apostrophes split suffixes off proper nouns; ts_debug shows every token's path.
SELECT alias, token, dictionary, lexemes
FROM ts_debug('turkish', 'TraceLite''ın raporu İstanbul''da');

CREATE TABLE requirements (id int PRIMARY KEY, title text NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO requirements VALUES
  (1, 'Giriş ekranında hata mesajı'),
  (2, 'Raporlama modülündeki hatalar'),
  (3, 'Hatay şubesi için yeni rapor');

-- Stems alone miss a form; prefixes on unstemmed words catch it, and more.
SELECT id, title,
       to_tsvector('turkish', title) @@ plainto_tsquery('turkish', 'hata') AS stem,
       to_tsvector('simple', title) @@ to_tsquery('simple', 'hata:*')      AS prefix
FROM requirements
ORDER BY id;

-- LEARN(sql.security-ops.roles): the sandbox role owns its database and nothing beyond it.
-- Role attributes are cluster-wide switches, separate from object privileges.
SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcreaterole, rolcreatedb, rolbypassrls
FROM pg_roles
WHERE rolname = current_user;

-- Roles whose privileges this session has without SET ROLE.
SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles
WHERE pg_has_role(current_user, oid, 'USAGE')
ORDER BY rolname;

-- Runs a statement and reports a permission error instead of aborting.
-- The EXCEPTION block is a subtransaction: a failure undoes only that statement.
CREATE FUNCTION try(stmt text) RETURNS text LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
  EXECUTE stmt;
  RETURN 'allowed';
EXCEPTION WHEN insufficient_privilege THEN
  RETURN SQLERRM;
END $$;

SELECT stmt AS "statement", try(stmt) AS outcome
FROM unnest(ARRAY[
  'CREATE ROLE tracelite_app LOGIN',
  'ALTER ROLE playground BYPASSRLS',
  'SET ROLE pg_read_all_stats',
  $$COPY (SELECT 1) TO PROGRAM 'whoami'$$,
  $$SELECT pg_read_file('postgresql.conf')$$,
  'SELECT rolpassword FROM pg_authid',
  'SET log_min_duration_statement = 0',
  'CREATE SCHEMA tracelite',
  'DROP SCHEMA public'
]) WITH ORDINALITY AS t (stmt, n)
ORDER BY n;

-- LEARN(sql.server-side.triggers): a BEFORE ROW trigger rewrites the row before it is stored.
CREATE TABLE requirements (
  id         int  PRIMARY KEY,
  title      text NOT NULL,
  status     text NOT NULL,
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
-- Pretend these rows were last changed a week ago.
INSERT INTO requirements VALUES
  (1, 'Kullanıcı girişi', 'draft',    '2026-11-06 09:00+03'),
  (2, 'CSV dışa aktarım', 'approved', '2026-11-06 09:00+03'),
  (3, 'Denetim izi',      'draft',    '2026-11-06 09:00+03');

CREATE FUNCTION set_updated_at() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
  NEW.updated_at := now();
  RETURN NEW;  -- the row to store; RETURN NULL would skip this row silently
END
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER requirements_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON requirements
  FOR EACH ROW
  WHEN (OLD.* IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.*)
  EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

UPDATE requirements SET status = 'approved' WHERE id = 1;        -- a real change
UPDATE requirements SET status = 'approved' WHERE id = 2;        -- same value
UPDATE requirements SET updated_at = '2000-01-01' WHERE id = 3;  -- a backdating client

SELECT id, status,
       updated_at = now() AS stamped_now,
       updated_at = '2026-11-06 09:00+03' AS kept_old_stamp
FROM requirements
ORDER BY id;

-- What the server has on disk, and what a non-superuser may load:
-- trusted = any role with CREATE on the database; otherwise superuser only.
SELECT v.name, v.trusted
FROM pg_available_extension_versions v
JOIN pg_available_extensions a ON a.name = v.name AND a.default_version = v.version
WHERE v.name IN ('pg_trgm', 'unaccent', 'btree_gist', 'tcn',
                 'pg_stat_statements', 'file_fdw', 'postgres_fdw')
ORDER BY v.trusted DESC, v.name;

-- Loading one runs its install script in this database, creating its
-- objects in the first schema on search_path (this run's own schema).
CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm;
CREATE EXTENSION unaccent;

SELECT e.extname,
       e.extowner::regrole AS owner,
       e.extnamespace::regnamespace::text = current_schema() AS in_this_schema,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_depend d
        WHERE d.refclassid = 'pg_extension'::regclass
          AND d.refobjid = e.oid AND d.deptype = 'e') AS member_objects
FROM pg_extension e
WHERE e.extname IN ('pg_trgm', 'unaccent')
ORDER BY e.extname;

-- New functions, operators and index support, usable at once.
CREATE TABLE requirements (code text PRIMARY KEY, title text NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO requirements VALUES
  ('REQ-1', 'Kullanıcı girişi şifre ile'),
  ('REQ-2', 'Şifre sıfırlama e-postası'),
  ('REQ-3', 'Raporu CSV olarak dışa aktar');
SELECT code, unaccent(title) AS plain,
       round(similarity(unaccent(lower(title)), 'sifre sifirlama')::numeric, 2) AS similarity
FROM requirements
ORDER BY similarity DESC, code;

-- gin_trgm_ops makes LIKE '%...%' indexable, which a B-tree can't do.
CREATE INDEX requirements_title_trgm ON requirements USING gin (title gin_trgm_ops);
SET LOCAL enable_seqscan = off;  -- three rows: make the planner show the index
EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF) SELECT code FROM requirements WHERE title ILIKE '%şifre%';

-- Untrusted: file_fdw reads files on the database server.
CREATE EXTENSION file_fdw;

package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"
	"time"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgconn"
)

func check(err error) {
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

// show prints what arrives on conn until it has been quiet for 300 ms.
func show(ctx context.Context, conn *pgx.Conn, label string) {
	fmt.Println(label)
	for {
		wctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 300*time.Millisecond)
		n, err := conn.WaitForNotification(wctx)
		cancel()
		if pgconn.Timeout(err) {
			return // quiet; the connection is still usable
		}
		check(err)
		fmt.Println("  " + n.Payload)
	}
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	writer, err := pgx.Connect(ctx, os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL"))
	check(err)
	defer writer.Close(ctx)
	listener, err := pgx.Connect(ctx, os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL"))
	check(err)
	defer listener.Close(ctx)
	exec := func(conn *pgx.Conn, sql string) {
		_, err := conn.Exec(ctx, sql)
		check(err)
	}

	// Channels are database-wide: name this run's after its own schema.
	var channel string
	check(writer.QueryRow(ctx, "SELECT current_schema() || '_changes'").Scan(&channel))
	exec(writer, "CREATE EXTENSION tcn") // trusted: no superuser needed
	exec(writer, "CREATE TABLE test_runs (id int PRIMARY KEY, status text NOT NULL)")
	exec(writer, `CREATE TRIGGER test_runs_tcn AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON test_runs
		FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION triggered_change_notification('`+channel+`')`)
	exec(listener, "LISTEN "+pgx.Identifier{channel}.Sanitize())

	tx, err := writer.Begin(ctx)
	check(err)
	_, err = tx.Exec(ctx, "INSERT INTO test_runs VALUES (1, 'running'), (2, 'running')")
	check(err)
	show(ctx, listener, "INSERT, not yet committed:")
	check(tx.Commit(ctx))
	show(ctx, listener, "after COMMIT:")

	exec(writer, "UPDATE test_runs SET status = 'passed' WHERE id = 1")
	exec(writer, "DELETE FROM test_runs WHERE id = 2")
	show(ctx, listener, "UPDATE, then DELETE:")

	exec(writer, "BEGIN; UPDATE test_runs SET status = 'failed'; ROLLBACK")
	show(ctx, listener, "rolled-back UPDATE:")
}

INSERT INTO test_runs VALUES
  (1, 10, 1, 120, true), (2, 10, 2, 900, false), (3, 10, 3, 110, true),
  (4, 11, 1, 300, false);

-- Uncorrelated: it doesn't mention the outer row, so it runs once and acts
-- as a constant.
SELECT id, duration_ms
FROM test_runs
WHERE duration_ms > (SELECT avg(duration_ms) FROM test_runs)
ORDER BY id;

-- Correlated: t.id comes from the outer row, so it is evaluated per test case.

       (SELECT count(*) FROM test_runs r WHERE r.test_case_id = t.id) AS runs,

        WHERE r.test_case_id = t.id
        ORDER BY r.run_no DESC LIMIT 1) AS last_passed
FROM test_cases t
ORDER BY t.id;

EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF)
SELECT t.title,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM test_runs r WHERE r.test_case_id = t.id) AS runs
FROM test_cases t;

-- Without ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 this fails, but only for test cases that
-- have more than one run. The others would have worked.

       (SELECT r.passed FROM test_runs r WHERE r.test_case_id = t.id) AS passed
FROM test_cases t
ORDER BY t.id;

CREATE TABLE test_cases (id int PRIMARY KEY, title text NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE test_runs (

  test_case_id int NOT NULL REFERENCES test_cases,
  passed       boolean NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO test_cases VALUES (10, 'Valid password'), (11, 'Locked account'), (12, 'Export CSV');
INSERT INTO test_runs VALUES
  (1, 10, true), (2, 10, false), (3, 10, true),
  (4, 11, false), (5, 11, false), (6, 12, true), (7, 12, false);

-- "Flaky tests": both passed and failed at least once. Nested derived
-- tables read inside-out, and the innermost step comes first.
SELECT t.title, f.passes, f.failures
FROM (
  SELECT test_case_id, passes, failures
  FROM (
    SELECT test_case_id,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE passed)     AS passes,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT passed) AS failures
    FROM test_runs
    GROUP BY test_case_id
  ) AS per_case
  WHERE passes > 0 AND failures > 0
) AS f
JOIN test_cases t ON t.id = f.test_case_id
ORDER BY t.title;

-- The same query as named steps, read top to bottom.
WITH per_case AS (
  SELECT test_case_id,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE passed)     AS passes,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT passed) AS failures
  FROM test_runs
  GROUP BY test_case_id
),
flaky AS (
  SELECT test_case_id, passes, failures
  FROM per_case
  WHERE passes > 0 AND failures > 0
)

FROM flaky f
JOIN test_cases t ON t.id = f.test_case_id
ORDER BY t.title;

CREATE TABLE test_runs (
  id           int PRIMARY KEY,
  test_case_id int NOT NULL,
  passed       boolean NOT NULL
);

-- Referenced once and free of side effects: inlined (PG 12+). The outer
-- WHERE reaches the table, so the primary key index can answer it.
EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF)
WITH failed AS (SELECT * FROM test_runs WHERE NOT passed)
SELECT * FROM failed WHERE id = 4;

-- MATERIALIZED: the CTE is computed on its own first, every failed run,
-- and the outer filter is applied to that result.
EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF)
WITH failed AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT * FROM test_runs WHERE NOT passed)
SELECT * FROM failed WHERE id = 4;

-- Referenced twice: materialized by default, computed once and read twice.
EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF)
WITH failed AS (SELECT * FROM test_runs WHERE NOT passed)
SELECT a.id, b.id
FROM failed a
JOIN failed b ON b.test_case_id = a.test_case_id AND b.id > a.id;

-- NOT MATERIALIZED inlines it anyway: two scans of test_runs, no CTE Scan.
EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF)
WITH failed AS NOT MATERIALIZED (SELECT * FROM test_runs WHERE NOT passed)
SELECT a.id, b.id
FROM failed a
JOIN failed b ON b.test_case_id = a.test_case_id AND b.id > a.id;

-- LEARN(sql.subqueries-ctes.recursive): the step query reruns on the last round's rows until none come back.
CREATE TABLE requirements (
  id        int PRIMARY KEY,
  parent_id int REFERENCES requirements,   -- NULL: a top-level requirement
  code      text NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO requirements VALUES
  (1, NULL, 'AUTH'), (2, 1, 'AUTH-LOGIN'), (3, 1, 'AUTH-RESET'),
  (4, 2, 'AUTH-LOGIN-2FA'), (5, 2, 'AUTH-LOGIN-LOCKOUT'),
  (6, NULL, 'EXPORT'), (7, 6, 'EXPORT-CSV');

-- Down the tree: AUTH and everything below it.
WITH RECURSIVE subtree AS (
  SELECT id, code, 0 AS depth              -- non-recursive term: the start
  FROM requirements
  WHERE code = 'AUTH'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.id, c.code, s.depth + 1         -- recursive term: children of
  FROM requirements c                      -- the rows found last round
  JOIN subtree s ON c.parent_id = s.id
) SEARCH DEPTH FIRST BY code SET ord
SELECT repeat('. ', depth) || code AS outline, depth
FROM subtree
ORDER BY ord;

-- Up the tree: the ancestors of one leaf, nearest first.
WITH RECURSIVE ancestors AS (
  SELECT id, parent_id, code, 0 AS up
  FROM requirements
  WHERE code = 'AUTH-LOGIN-2FA'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT p.id, p.parent_id, p.code, a.up + 1
  FROM requirements p
  JOIN ancestors a ON p.id = a.parent_id
)
SELECT up, code
FROM ancestors
ORDER BY up;

-- Links from stakeholder needs (STK) to system requirements (SYS) to test
-- cases (TC) form a graph: TC-10 verifies two requirements, and a careless
-- link closes a loop (SYS-2 and SYS-3 point at each other).
CREATE TABLE trace_links (
  from_code text NOT NULL,
  to_code   text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (from_code, to_code)
);
INSERT INTO trace_links VALUES
  ('STK-1', 'SYS-1'), ('STK-1', 'SYS-2'),
  ('SYS-1', 'TC-10'), ('SYS-2', 'TC-10'), ('SYS-2', 'TC-11'),
  ('SYS-2', 'SYS-3'), ('SYS-3', 'SYS-2');

-- Naive: UNION ALL with no cycle check would never stop on this data.
-- A depth guard stops it, after the loop has repeated rows up to the guard.
WITH RECURSIVE reach AS (
  SELECT 'STK-1'::text AS code, 0 AS hops
  UNION ALL
  SELECT l.to_code, r.hops + 1
  FROM reach r
  JOIN trace_links l ON l.from_code = r.code
  WHERE r.hops < 6
)
SELECT code, count(*) AS times_reached
FROM reach
GROUP BY code
ORDER BY code;

-- CYCLE (PG 14) tracks the path and stops at a node already on it.
WITH RECURSIVE reach AS (
  SELECT 'STK-1'::text AS code, 0 AS hops
  UNION ALL
  SELECT l.to_code, r.hops + 1
  FROM reach r
  JOIN trace_links l ON l.from_code = r.code
) CYCLE code SET is_cycle USING path
SELECT hops, code, is_cycle, path
FROM reach
ORDER BY path;

-- Only need the set of reachable nodes? UNION discards rows it has already
-- produced, so the loop runs dry on its own.
WITH RECURSIVE reach(code) AS (
  SELECT 'STK-1'::text
  UNION
  SELECT l.to_code
  FROM reach r
  JOIN trace_links l ON l.from_code = r.code
)
SELECT code FROM reach ORDER BY code;

CREATE TABLE requirements (
  id        int PRIMARY KEY,
  parent_id int REFERENCES requirements,
  code      text NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE test_cases (id int PRIMARY KEY, last_passed boolean NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE trace_links (
  requirement_id int REFERENCES requirements,
  test_case_id   int REFERENCES test_cases,
  PRIMARY KEY (requirement_id, test_case_id)
);
INSERT INTO requirements VALUES
  (1, NULL, 'AUTH'), (2, 1, 'AUTH-LOGIN'), (3, 1, 'AUTH-RESET'),
  (4, 2, 'AUTH-LOGIN-2FA'), (6, NULL, 'EXPORT'), (7, 6, 'EXPORT-CSV');
INSERT INTO test_cases VALUES (10, true), (11, false), (12, true);
-- Test 10 verifies two requirements in the same subtree.
INSERT INTO trace_links VALUES (2, 10), (4, 10), (4, 11), (3, 12);

-- Tag every requirement with its top-level ancestor by carrying the root's
-- id down the tree, then aggregate the linked tests per root.
WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (
  SELECT id, id AS root_id FROM requirements WHERE parent_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT c.id, t.root_id
  FROM requirements c
  JOIN tree t ON c.parent_id = t.id
)
SELECT root.code,
       count(l.test_case_id)          AS links,
       count(DISTINCT l.test_case_id) AS tests,
       count(DISTINCT l.test_case_id) FILTER (WHERE NOT tc.last_passed) AS failing
FROM tree
JOIN requirements root  ON root.id = tree.root_id
LEFT JOIN trace_links l ON l.requirement_id = tree.id
LEFT JOIN test_cases tc ON tc.id = l.test_case_id
GROUP BY root.id
ORDER BY root.code;

-- date is a calendar day (4 bytes). date - date is a whole number of days.
SELECT date '2026-11-13' - date '2026-01-01' AS days_since_new_year,
       date '2026-11-13' + 7 AS one_week_later;

-- interval keeps months, days and microseconds apart, because months and
-- days have no fixed length. Month arithmetic clamps to the month's end.
SELECT date '2026-01-31' + interval '1 month' AS jan31_plus_1_month,
       age(date '2026-11-13', date '1990-05-20') AS age;

-- Turkey has had no DST since 2016, but Berlin moves its clocks from 02:00
-- to 03:00 on 2026-03-29, so that calendar day is 23 hours long.
SET TimeZone = 'Europe/Berlin';
SELECT timestamptz '2026-03-28 12:00' + interval '1 day'   AS plus_1_day,
       timestamptz '2026-03-28 12:00' + interval '24 hours' AS plus_24_hours,
       timestamptz '2026-03-29 12:00' - timestamptz '2026-03-28 12:00' AS elapsed;

-- now() is the transaction's start time, the same in every statement of it.
-- clock_timestamp() reads the clock each time it is called.
SELECT now() = transaction_timestamp() AS now_is_tx_start,
       clock_timestamp() > now() AS clock_has_moved_on;

CREATE TABLE events (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),  -- time-ordered (PostgreSQL 18)
  n  int  NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE events_v4 (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv4(),  -- random; same as gen_random_uuid()
  n  int  NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO events    (n) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1, 1000) AS g;
INSERT INTO events_v4 (n) SELECT g FROM generate_series(1, 1000) AS g;

-- Generated ids differ on every run, so look at their properties.
-- Does ORDER BY id give back the insertion order?
SELECT 'uuidv7' AS generator,
       array_agg(n ORDER BY id) = array_agg(n ORDER BY n) AS id_order_is_insert_order
FROM events
UNION ALL
SELECT 'uuidv4', array_agg(n ORDER BY id) = array_agg(n ORDER BY n)
FROM events_v4
ORDER BY generator;

-- A v7 id carries its creation time; a v4 id carries nothing but randomness.
SELECT uuid_extract_version(v7) AS v7_version,
       uuid_extract_timestamp(v7) BETWEEN now() - interval '1 minute'
                                      AND now() + interval '1 minute' AS v7_time_is_now,
       uuid_extract_version(v4) AS v4_version,
       uuid_extract_timestamp(v4) AS v4_time
FROM (SELECT uuidv7() AS v7, uuidv4() AS v4) AS ids;

-- 16 bytes as uuid, 36 characters as text. And shift backdates the
-- embedded time, e.g. when backfilling ids for historic rows.
SELECT pg_column_size(uuidv7()) AS uuid_bytes,
       length(uuidv7()::text) AS text_chars,
       uuidv7(interval '-1 day') < (SELECT id FROM events ORDER BY id LIMIT 1) AS backdated_sorts_first;

-- duplicates dropped (the last one wins).
SELECT '{"b": 1, "a": 2, "a": 3}'::json  AS as_json,
       '{"b": 1, "a": 2, "a": 3}'::jsonb AS as_jsonb;

CREATE TABLE products (
  sku   text PRIMARY KEY,
  name  text NOT NULL,
  price numeric(10, 2) NOT NULL,     -- every product has one: a real column
  attrs jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'  -- differs per category: jsonb
);

INSERT INTO products VALUES
  ('tea-rize', 'Rize çayı',   249.90, '{"origin": "Rize", "weight_g": 1000}'),
  ('tea-earl', 'Earl Grey',   189.50, '{"origin": "Sri Lanka", "weight_g": 250, "organic": true}'),
  ('usb-c',    'USB-C kablo', 129.00, '{"length_m": 2, "watts": 100}');

-- -> returns jsonb, ->> returns text. @> asks "does attrs contain this
-- document?", ? asks "does it have this key?".
SELECT sku, attrs -> 'weight_g' AS weight_json, attrs ->> 'origin' AS origin
FROM products
WHERE attrs @> '{"origin": "Rize"}' OR attrs ? 'organic'
ORDER BY sku;

-- Nothing checks the shape of a jsonb value, so this insert succeeds...
INSERT INTO products VALUES
  ('tea-green', 'Yeşil çay', 99.00, '{"origin": "Rize", "weight_g": "yarım kilo"}');

-- ...and the mistake surfaces later, in somebody else's report.
SELECT sum((attrs ->> 'weight_g')::int) AS total_tea_grams
FROM products
WHERE sku LIKE 'tea-%';

CREATE TABLE articles (
  id    int    PRIMARY KEY,
  title text   NOT NULL,
  tags  text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
);

INSERT INTO articles VALUES
  (1, 'Goroutines in practice', ARRAY['go', 'concurrency']),
  (2, 'timestamptz explained',  ARRAY['sql', 'time']),
  (3, 'pgx and transactions',   ARRAY['go', 'sql']),
  (4, 'Draft',                  '{}');

-- Arrays are 1-based, and reading outside the bounds yields NULL, not an
-- error. For an empty array, array_length() is NULL and cardinality() is 0.
SELECT id, tags[1] AS first, tags[0] AS index_zero, tags[3] AS past_end,
       array_length(tags, 1) AS array_length, cardinality(tags) AS cardinality
FROM articles
ORDER BY id;

-- Membership: = ANY for one value, @> for "contains all of these".
SELECT id, title FROM articles WHERE 'sql' = ANY (tags) ORDER BY id;
SELECT id, title FROM articles WHERE tags @> ARRAY['go', 'sql'] ORDER BY id;

-- unnest turns an array back into rows: articles per tag.
SELECT tag, count(*) AS articles
FROM articles, unnest(tags) AS tag
GROUP BY tag
ORDER BY tag;

UPDATE articles SET tags = array_append(tags, 'golang') WHERE id = 1
RETURNING id, tags;

-- Claim in one short transaction, work outside it, finish in another.
-- A's claim is still open when B claims, so B skips job 1.
A: BEGIN;
A: UPDATE jobs SET status = 'running', attempts = attempts + 1,
                  lease_until = now() + interval '5 minutes'
   WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE status = 'queued'
               ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)
   RETURNING id, kind, attempts;
B: UPDATE jobs SET status = 'running', attempts = attempts + 1,
                  lease_until = now() + interval '5 minutes'
   WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE status = 'queued'
               ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)
   RETURNING id, kind, attempts;
A: COMMIT;

-- B does the work, then finishes in a second short transaction.
B: UPDATE jobs SET status = 'done', lease_until = NULL WHERE id = 2;

-- A dies while working. Its claim is committed, so nothing rolls back:
-- job 1 stays 'running' until its lease runs out. (Demo only: expire it now.)
B: UPDATE jobs SET lease_until = now() - interval '1 second' WHERE id = 1;

-- The reaper, run by any worker now and then, puts expired jobs back.
B: UPDATE jobs SET status = 'queued', lease_until = NULL
   WHERE status = 'running' AND lease_until < now()
   RETURNING id, attempts;

-- The next claim gets job 1 again; attempts says it is the second try.
B: UPDATE jobs SET status = 'running', attempts = attempts + 1,
                  lease_until = now() + interval '5 minutes'
   WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE status = 'queued'
               ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED)
   RETURNING id, kind, attempts;

-- LEARN(sql.windows.over): a window function computes over related rows and keeps every row.
CREATE TABLE test_runs (
  id          int  PRIMARY KEY,
  suite       text NOT NULL,
  test_case   text NOT NULL,
  duration_ms int  NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO test_runs VALUES
  (1, 'auth',   'Giriş',            120),
  (2, 'auth',   'Çıkış',             80),
  (3, 'auth',   'Şifre sıfırlama',  400),
  (4, 'export', 'CSV dışa aktarım', 900),
  (5, 'export', 'PDF rapor',        300);

-- GROUP BY collapses each suite into one row; the tests are gone.
SELECT suite, count(*) AS runs, sum(duration_ms) AS suite_ms
FROM test_runs
GROUP BY suite
ORDER BY suite;

-- The same aggregates with OVER keep every row and attach the group's figures.
SELECT suite, test_case, duration_ms,
       count(*)         OVER (PARTITION BY suite) AS runs,
       sum(duration_ms) OVER (PARTITION BY suite) AS suite_ms,
       round(100.0 * duration_ms / sum(duration_ms) OVER (PARTITION BY suite), 1)
                                                  AS pct_of_suite,
       sum(duration_ms) OVER ()                   AS all_ms
FROM test_runs
ORDER BY suite, id;

-- Filtering on a window result needs a subquery: compute first, filter outside.
SELECT suite, test_case, duration_ms, suite_avg
FROM (
  SELECT suite, test_case, duration_ms,
         round(avg(duration_ms) OVER (PARTITION BY suite)) AS suite_avg
  FROM test_runs
) AS t
WHERE duration_ms > suite_avg
ORDER BY suite, test_case;

-- WHERE runs before any window is computed, so it can't refer to one.
SELECT test_case FROM test_runs
WHERE duration_ms > avg(duration_ms) OVER (PARTITION BY suite);
CREATE TABLE test_cases (
  id          int  PRIMARY KEY,
  suite       text NOT NULL,
  title       text NOT NULL,
  duration_ms int  NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO test_cases VALUES
  (1, 'auth',   'Oturum süresi',        300),
  (2, 'auth',   'Giriş',                300),
  (3, 'auth',   'İki adımlı doğrulama', 500),
  (4, 'auth',   'Çıkış',                300),
  (5, 'auth',   'Şifre sıfırlama',      200),
  (6, 'export', 'CSV dışa aktarım',     900),
  (7, 'export', 'PDF rapor',            900);

-- Slowest first in each suite. Three tests tie at 300 ms: rank and
-- dense_rank give them one number, row_number needs a tie-breaker.
SELECT suite, title, duration_ms,
       rank()       OVER by_time AS rank,
       dense_rank() OVER by_time AS dense_rank,
       row_number() OVER (per_suite ORDER BY duration_ms DESC,
                          title COLLATE "tr-x-icu") AS row_number
FROM test_cases
WINDOW per_suite AS (PARTITION BY suite),
       by_time   AS (per_suite ORDER BY duration_ms DESC)
ORDER BY suite, row_number;

-- Windows run after GROUP BY, so they can rank the groups themselves.
SELECT suite, sum(duration_ms) AS suite_ms,
       rank() OVER (ORDER BY sum(duration_ms) DESC) AS slowest
FROM test_cases
GROUP BY suite
ORDER BY slowest, suite;

SET TimeZone = 'Europe/Istanbul';

CREATE TABLE test_runs (
  id          int         PRIMARY KEY,
  test_case   text        NOT NULL,
  ran_at      timestamptz NOT NULL,
  status      text        NOT NULL,
  duration_ms int         NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO test_runs VALUES
  (1, 'Giriş', '2026-11-10 09:00+03', 'passed', 120),
  (2, 'Giriş', '2026-11-11 09:00+03', 'passed', 130),
  (3, 'Giriş', '2026-11-12 09:00+03', 'failed', 940),
  (4, 'Giriş', '2026-11-13 09:00+03', 'passed', 125),
  (5, 'Çıkış', '2026-11-11 18:30+03', 'failed',  80),
  (6, 'Çıkış', '2026-11-13 09:05+03', 'failed',  85);

-- Each run next to the previous and next run of the same test case.
SELECT test_case, ran_at::date AS day, status,
       lag(status) OVER w                    AS prev_status,
       lag(status, 1, 'first run') OVER w    AS prev_or_label,
       duration_ms - lag(duration_ms) OVER w AS delta_ms,
       lead(ran_at) OVER w - ran_at          AS until_next_run
FROM test_runs
WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY test_case ORDER BY ran_at, id)
ORDER BY test_case, ran_at, id;

-- Regressions: a run that failed right after a pass of the same test.
SELECT test_case, ran_at
FROM (
  SELECT test_case, ran_at, status,

-- LEARN(sql.windows.frames): the frame decides which rows an aggregate OVER (...) sees.
CREATE TABLE runs (
  id      int  PRIMARY KEY,
  project text NOT NULL,
  ran_on  date NOT NULL,
  failed  int  NOT NULL          -- failed tests in this run
);
INSERT INTO runs VALUES
  (1, 'TraceLite', '2026-11-09', 3),
  (2, 'TraceLite', '2026-11-10', 1),
  (3, 'TraceLite', '2026-11-10', 4),   -- a second run on the same day
  (4, 'TraceLite', '2026-11-12', 2),
  (5, 'StackLab',  '2026-11-10', 5),
  (6, 'StackLab',  '2026-11-11', 0);

-- ORDER BY inside OVER turns sum into a running sum. The default frame
-- (RANGE) ends at the current row's last peer; ROWS ends at the row itself.
SELECT project, ran_on, id, failed,
       sum(failed) OVER (PARTITION BY project ORDER BY ran_on) AS range_default,
       sum(failed) OVER (PARTITION BY project ORDER BY ran_on, id
                         ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)             AS rows_running,
       sum(failed) OVER (PARTITION BY project)                 AS project_total
FROM runs
ORDER BY project, ran_on, id;

-- last_value sees the frame, not the partition: with the default frame the
-- "last" row is the current one. Widen the frame to get the latest run.
SELECT project, id, failed,
       last_value(failed) OVER (PARTITION BY project ORDER BY ran_on, id)
         AS last_default,
       last_value(failed) OVER (PARTITION BY project ORDER BY ran_on, id
                                ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
                                         AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
         AS latest_failed
FROM runs
ORDER BY project, id;

CREATE TABLE nightly_builds (
  built_on date PRIMARY KEY,
  minutes  int  NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO nightly_builds VALUES
  ('2026-11-02', 10), ('2026-11-03', 12), ('2026-11-04', 11),
  ('2026-11-05', 30), ('2026-11-06', 13),
  -- no builds on the weekend of 11-07 and 11-08
  ('2026-11-09', 14), ('2026-11-10', 12);

-- "Last three builds" (ROWS) vs "last three days" (RANGE with an interval).
-- count(*) over the same frame shows how many rows each average used.
SELECT built_on, minutes,
       round(avg(minutes) OVER last3_rows, 1) AS avg_3_builds,
       count(*)           OVER last3_rows     AS n_builds,
       round(avg(minutes) OVER last3_days, 1) AS avg_3_days,
       count(*)           OVER last3_days     AS n_days
FROM nightly_builds
WINDOW last3_rows AS (ORDER BY built_on ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW),
       last3_days AS (ORDER BY built_on
                      RANGE BETWEEN '2 days' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
ORDER BY built_on;

-- A baseline that excludes the current row: the three builds before it.
SELECT built_on, minutes, baseline,
       minutes > 2 * baseline AS spike
FROM (
  SELECT built_on, minutes,
         round(avg(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY built_on
                                  ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING), 1)
           AS baseline
  FROM nightly_builds
) AS b
ORDER BY built_on;

-- RANGE with an offset measures distance on one value, so it needs exactly
-- one ORDER BY column.
SELECT built_on,
       avg(minutes) OVER (ORDER BY built_on, minutes
                          RANGE BETWEEN '2 days' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
FROM nightly_builds;

-- LEARN(sql.windows.gaps-islands): number the rows, subtract, and consecutive rows share a key.
CREATE TABLE uploads (
  day date PRIMARY KEY            -- days the CI agent uploaded its results
);
INSERT INTO uploads VALUES
  ('2026-11-01'), ('2026-11-02'), ('2026-11-03'),
  ('2026-11-06'), ('2026-11-07'),
  ('2026-11-10'), ('2026-11-11'), ('2026-11-12'), ('2026-11-13');

-- Gaps: look at the next day; a jump of more than one day is a hole.
SELECT day + 1 AS gap_from, next_day - 1 AS gap_to,
       next_day - day - 1 AS missing_days
FROM (SELECT day, lead(day) OVER (ORDER BY day) AS next_day FROM uploads) AS d
WHERE next_day - day > 1
ORDER BY gap_from;

-- Islands: day and row number both grow by 1 inside a streak, so their
-- difference stays constant until a gap shifts it.
SELECT day,
       row_number() OVER (ORDER BY day) AS rn,
       day - row_number() OVER (ORDER BY day)::int AS island
FROM uploads
ORDER BY day;

-- Group on that constant: one row per streak.
SELECT min(day) AS first_day, max(day) AS last_day, count(*) AS days
FROM (
  SELECT day, day - row_number() OVER (ORDER BY day)::int AS island
  FROM uploads
) AS s
GROUP BY island
ORDER BY first_day;

CREATE TABLE test_runs (
  test_case text NOT NULL,
  build     int  NOT NULL,           -- CI build number; not every build runs every test
  status    text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (test_case, build)
);
INSERT INTO test_runs VALUES
  ('Giriş', 101, 'passed'), ('Giriş', 102, 'passed'), ('Giriş', 103, 'failed'),
  ('Giriş', 104, 'failed'), ('Giriş', 105, 'passed'), ('Giriş', 106, 'passed'),
  ('Çıkış', 101, 'passed'), ('Çıkış', 103, 'failed'), ('Çıkış', 105, 'failed'),
  ('Çıkış', 106, 'failed');

-- Step 1: flag each row that differs from the previous one (lag), and
-- step 2: a running sum of the flags numbers the islands.
CREATE VIEW numbered AS
SELECT test_case, build, status, starts,
       sum(starts) OVER (PARTITION BY test_case ORDER BY build) AS island
FROM (
  SELECT test_case, build, status,
         CASE WHEN status IS DISTINCT FROM
                   lag(status) OVER (PARTITION BY test_case ORDER BY build)
              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS starts
  FROM test_runs
) AS flagged;

SELECT * FROM numbered ORDER BY test_case, build;

-- Step 3: one row per island, and the current streak of each test.
SELECT test_case, status, min(build) AS from_build, max(build) AS to_build,
       count(*) AS runs,
       island = max(island) OVER (PARTITION BY test_case) AS current
FROM numbered
GROUP BY test_case, island, status
ORDER BY test_case, from_build;

-- The tempting one-step version: lag inside sum() OVER.
SELECT test_case, build,
       sum(CASE WHEN status <> lag(status) OVER w THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER w
FROM test_runs
WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY test_case ORDER BY build);

SET TimeZone = 'Europe/Istanbul';

CREATE TABLE ui_events (
  id      int         PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id text        NOT NULL,
  at      timestamptz NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO ui_events VALUES
  (1, 'ayşe',  '2026-11-13 09:00+03'), (2, 'ayşe',  '2026-11-13 09:20+03'),
  (3, 'ayşe',  '2026-11-13 09:45+03'), (4, 'ayşe',  '2026-11-13 10:10+03'),
  (5, 'ayşe',  '2026-11-13 14:00+03'), (6, 'ayşe',  '2026-11-13 14:05+03'),
  (7, 'emre',  '2026-11-13 09:00+03'), (8, 'emre',  '2026-11-13 09:31+03');

-- A session ends after 30 minutes of silence. Islands again, but the
-- break condition is a time gap instead of a changed value.
SELECT user_id, session_no,
       min(at)::time AS started, max(at)::time AS ended,
       max(at) - min(at) AS length, count(*) AS events
FROM (
  SELECT user_id, at,
         sum(new_session) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY at, id) AS session_no
  FROM (
    SELECT user_id, at, id,
           CASE WHEN at - lag(at) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY at, id)
                     <= interval '30 minutes'
                THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS new_session
    FROM ui_events
  ) AS flagged
) AS sessions
GROUP BY user_id, session_no
ORDER BY user_id, session_no;
